intro: Azerbaijan stretches from the Caucasus mountains to the Caspian Sea, the largest lake on Earth.

chapters.title: Mountains, plains and sea
text: The Greater Caucasus rises in the north, with Bazarduzu the highest peak at 4,466 m. The Kura river crosses wide lowlands, some below sea level. The Absheron peninsula, with Baku, juts into the Caspian.
Azerbaijan has around half the world's mud volcanoes.

chapters.title: Nakhchivan
text: The Nakhchivan exclave is separated from the rest of the country by Armenia.

keyTerms.meaning: Part of a country cut off from the rest by another country's land.
